leadIn:
I’m using the active settle workflow: I’ll first trace the export flow and its writers/tests, then bring only genuinely user-owned behavior choices back through the native question form before touching code.

This is a **bounded** change: the existing export/cache flow owns the behavior; no new API, schema, or subsystem is required.

Verified facts:

- `src/cache.js` gives every cached range a six-hour TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_MS`), while `README.md` says upstream rewrites `data/orders.json` about every 15 minutes.
- `src/exporter.js` returns the range cache without checking whether the source file changed.
- `README.md` says the nightly job depends on caching to complete within ten minutes, but explicitly leaves ad-hoc freshness undecided.
- `test/exporter.test.js` protects only the exact CSV column order; it has no cache freshness or recovery coverage.

**Inference:** the stale reports come from time-only invalidation. Comparing the cache file with the source file can preserve reuse across the ~400 nightly calls while invalidating ranges after a sync.

**Dependency map:** freshness policy determines invalidation; source-failure policy determines whether an invalidated cache remains a fallback; corrupt-cache behavior then shapes recovery tests.

questions.question: When upstream data has changed, what should the next export show? A wrong choice either preserves stale ad-hoc reports or weakens the nightly performance guarantee. Evidence: `src/cache.js` uses a six-hour TTL; `README.md` says source updates arrive about every 15 minutes and nightly relies on cache speed.

options.label: Latest sync (Recommended)
options.description: Invalidate cached ranges after the source changes; adds one cheap filesystem metadata check per invocation.

options.label: Six-hour cache
options.description: Preserve current nightly-oriented behavior; ad-hoc exports can remain stale for up to six hours.

options.label: Separate modes
options.description: Add a caller-selected fresh/nightly behavior; clearer control, but changes the CLI contract and nightly invocation.

questions.question: If a newly rewritten `data/orders.json` is unreadable or malformed but an older valid cache exists, what should users receive? A wrong choice can silently serve stale finance data or make exports unavailable. Evidence: `src/store.js` currently throws on unreadable or invalid JSON, while a still-valid cache in `src/exporter.js` can mask it.

options.label: Fail clearly (Recommended)
options.description: Exit nonzero instead of silently exporting old rows; exports are unavailable until upstream is repaired.

options.label: Use stale cache
options.description: Keep exports available from the last cached rows; consumers may not know the data is stale.

questions.question: If a cache file is malformed but the source is valid, should export recover or fail? A wrong choice trades resilience against surfacing local corruption. Evidence: `readCache` in `src/cache.js` currently lets JSON parse errors abort the command.

options.label: Rebuild cache (Recommended)
options.description: Read the valid source and replace the broken cache; local cache corruption is automatically healed.

options.label: Fail clearly
options.description: Expose cache corruption immediately; a valid report is blocked until the cache is removed manually.

leadIn:
The first round settles the core policy:

- **Freshness — user:** invalidate cached ranges after the source changes.
- **Malformed/unreadable source — user:** fail clearly; do not silently fall back to stale rows.
- **Malformed cache — user:** rebuild it from valid source data.

More verified facts:

- `loadOrders()` and cache I/O are synchronous (`src/store.js`, `src/cache.js`), but the upstream job can rewrite the source independently (`README.md`).
- Cache files are written directly to their final path (`src/cache.js`), so overlapping reportkit processes targeting the same range can observe one another’s writes.
- The repository contains no other source writer, cache reader, scheduler, or CLI mode; the external upstream/nightly jobs are described only in `README.md`.

**Open tension:** “latest sync” still needs a precise boundary when the source changes during one export, and overlapping processes need an observable outcome.

**Dependency map:** the mid-run rule determines whether an export retries; the overlap rule determines whether cache publication must be atomic. Both precede the final contract and tests.

questions.question: If upstream completes a valid newer rewrite while an export is already running, which snapshot should that export return? A wrong choice can violate the intended freshness boundary or add retry behavior. Evidence: `src/store.js` reads synchronously, while `README.md` identifies an independent upstream writer.

options.label: Restart newer (Recommended)
options.description: Detect the change and retry so the completed export reflects the newest sync; a continuously changing source may eventually fail after a bounded retry.

options.label: Finish started
options.description: Return the snapshot the export began reading; it may be one sync behind immediately after completion.

questions.question: When two reportkit processes export the same range concurrently, what should users observe? A wrong choice can leave a corrupt shared cache or unnecessarily reject valid work. Evidence: `src/cache.js` currently writes both processes directly to the same final cache path.

options.label: Both succeed (Recommended)
options.description: Publish cache files atomically so both exports complete; duplicate source work can occur on a cache miss.

options.label: Refuse overlap
options.description: Allow only one same-range export at a time; callers must retry and locking adds operational cleanup concerns.

leadIn:
The overlap decisions are now closed:

- **Mid-run source update — user:** finish from the snapshot the export started with; the next invocation sees the newer sync.
- **Concurrent same-range exports — user:** both succeed; cache publication must not expose a half-written file.

Repository evidence closes the remaining data-shape questions: filtering/mapping preserves empty, duplicate, and repeated rows (`src/store.js`, `src/exporter.js`); the CSV header is fixed and tested (`test/exporter.test.js`); and only reportkit reads `.reportkit-cache` in this repository. Old cache files can remain compatible because freshness can be determined from file timestamps without changing their JSON schema.

**Open tension:** “fail clearly” does not yet specify the CLI-visible error shape. That choice controls whether errors remain Node stack traces or become a stable operator-facing message and exit status.

**Dependency map:** this last failure-contract choice determines the CLI test; after it, I can present the complete contract for confirmation.

questions.question: How should source/cache failures appear at the CLI? A wrong choice either exposes implementation stacks to operators or hides debugging detail. Evidence: `src/cli.js` has no error handling today, so thrown read/parse errors produce a Node stack and nonzero exit.

options.label: Concise stderr (Recommended)
options.description: Print one reportkit-prefixed error and exit nonzero; stack detail is omitted from normal CLI output.

options.label: Node stack
options.description: Keep full uncaught exception detail for debugging; operator output remains noisy and implementation-specific.

leadIn:
All user-owned probes are closed:

- Freshness: next invocation after a source rewrite uses the latest sync.
- Invalid source: fail rather than serve a stale cache.
- Invalid cache: rebuild from the valid source.
- Mid-run rewrite: finish the snapshot already started; freshness applies on the next invocation.
- Same-range overlap: both commands succeed without exposing partial cache content.
- CLI failure: emit a concise `reportkit:` error on stderr and exit nonzero.

Resolved contract: reportkit will retain its existing `reportkit <from> <to>` interface and exact `id,placedAt,total,status` order. Cache entries remain reusable while both TTL-valid and no older than `data/orders.json`; cache publication becomes atomic. Existing cache JSON stays readable. Explicitly excluded are a new fresh/nightly flag, changes to source or CSV schemas, silent stale fallback, and changes to the external jobs. Focused tests will prove source-change invalidation, cache reuse, corrupt-cache recovery, invalid-source failure, overlap-safe publication, concise CLI errors, and stable columns; then `node --test` must pass.

**Inference:** these rules resolve the symptom without sacrificing the nightly cache’s repeated-read benefit. Implementation and the decision record wait only on confirmation that this contract is complete.

questions.question: Is this resolved contract complete and correct? Confirming authorizes implementation; rejecting it returns us to the specific missing or wrong decision.

options.label: Implement (Recommended)
options.description: Build and verify exactly this contract; excludes new CLI modes and schema changes.

options.label: Revise contract
options.description: Pause implementation and provide the missing or incorrect behavior through the free-form response.
